name: Front Foot Elevated Reverse Lunge
description: The front-foot elevated reverse lunge places the working foot on a slight elevation (a plate or low step), increasing the range of motion as the rear knee descends below the level of the front foot. This creates greater hip flexion and quad stretch on the working leg while also increasing glute recruitment. It bridges the gap between a standard reverse lunge and the Bulgarian split squat in terms of difficulty and range of motion.

execution.starting_position: Stand on a weight plate or low step (1-3 inches high) with the working foot. Hold dumbbells at the sides if loading.
execution.setup_instructions: Place a single weight plate flat on the floor. Stand on it with both feet, then step one foot back off the plate to perform the reverse lunge.
steps: Step 1: Stand on the elevation with the working foot. Step one foot back into a reverse lunge stance.
Step 2: Lower the rear knee directly down toward the floor, allowing it to descend below the level of the elevated front foot.
Step 3: The front foot knee bends deeply as the rear knee approaches the floor.
Step 4: Drive through the front foot to return to the starting position. Alternate legs each rep.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on the descent, exhale on the drive.
common_mistakes: Front foot rolling off the edge of the elevation
Rear knee touching and resting on the floor
safety_considerations: Ensure the elevation surface is stable and non-slip
Master the standard reverse lunge before adding a deficit
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Rear knee should travel to or near the floor below the front foot level.
coaching_cues: Front foot stays centered on the elevation
Drive up through the front heel
